questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find the information I needed. The university provided clear instructions before and upon arrival, and the orientation sessions answered most of my questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended an orientation day where we received information about the university, practical matters, and student life. After the information session, we were given a campus tour, followed by social activities

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university had a partnership with a housing provider that offered student accommodation on campus, close to the university. There were several housing options available. I lived in a shared dorm where I had my own room and private bathroom, but shared a kitchen with 13 other students

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Since I lived in a shared kitchen, I cooked most of my own meals

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to share the facilities with a lot of other students. I shared a kitchen with 13 people, so it could get quite messy, and the cleaning wasn't always the best. On the other hand, it was a great way to get to know other students

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process took place in several steps. First, we had to apply for pre-approval at the host institution of our courses before we knew the timetable. Once the courses were approved, we could register for them when the enrolment period opened. However, we only received the timetable at that point, so if any courses overlapped, we had to apply for pre-approval again before changing our course selection

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was some meetings

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I had originally hoped to take were either not offered or overlapped with other classes, which was a bit disappointing since they were part of the reason I chose Amsterdam. However, after making a few changes, I ended up with a set of courses that I was happy with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for pre-approval as early as possible, as the registration process takes place in several stages and you may need to make changes if your courses overlap or are not offered. It is also a good idea to have a few backup courses in case your first choices are not available

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level of the courses was very similar to what I am used to at my home university. The courses are offered at different levels, which gives you a good idea of their difficulty

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite similar to UCPH, with a combination of lectures and smaller tutorial classes. Some courses only had lectures, especially if the class size was smaller. One difference was that there was more group work, and in most cases you were assigned to a group rather than choosing your own. The assessment methods were also different. Instead of having most of the grade based on a single final exam, the final grade was usually made up of several assessments throughout the course, such as midterms, presentations, assignments, and a final exam

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Science Communication for Researchers. The course focuses on how to communicate scientific research to different audiences using different methods. You also get to choose topics within your own field of study. 
I would also recommend Ethics of Public Health. The course covered a range of ethical issues, such as organ donation and mandatory vaccination. It included many interesting discussions and gave different perspectives on current public health topics

questions.answer: ESN VU organised a variety of social activities throughout the semester, which was a great way to meet new people, especially during the first few weeks of the exchange

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam has a lot to offer, so I would recommend spending time exploring the city. It is also easy to visit other Dutch cities by train

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. The culture is quite similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in class

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The international environment and the cycling culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for a different assessment structure and a high academic level
Amsterdam is an amazing city to study abroad in

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a different assessment structure than at UCPH. The academic level is high, and most courses include several assessments throughout the semester, such as midterms, presentations, assignments, and a final exam. It is not unusual for students to find this challenging at first, so be prepared for busy exam periods

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from different countries and learning about each other's cultures

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the different assessment structure
